narrative:
The model determined that you have a 35% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, your credit history, and the amount you requested. Your checking account status of 0-200 DM was the single biggest reason for the denial. Most approved applicants (59%) have no checking account at all or maintain higher balances, so your relatively low balance pushed the prediction noticeably toward higher risk.

Your credit history of having critical or other existing credits worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval. This is actually a common and relatively positive history among applicants. However, it was not strong enough to overcome the other factors.

The loan amount of 3,617 DM also increased your risk score because it sits above the average request of approved applicants (about 3,020 DM). Taken together, these elements led the model to conclude that the overall risk was too high.

You should focus on building a stronger checking account balance over the next few months and consider applying for a smaller loan amount once your finances show more stability. This combination would likely improve your chances on a future application. (218 words)
